title: How a public library lends books
lead: A library keeps one record for every copy it owns, sets a due date when a copy leaves the desk, and holds returned copies for the next member in line.

tabs.label: Borrowing
tabs.title: Borrowing a book
tabs.lead: A member finds a title in the catalog, picks up a copy, and leaves with a due date.

blocks.text: The catalog lists each title once and every copy under it. A member searches by title, author, or subject and sees which branch has a copy and whether it is on the shelf.

items.text: One entry per book, with author, subject, and year
One physical book with its own barcode and home branch
On the shelf, checked out, on hold, or in transit

blocks.caption: Figure 1 How a request moves from the catalog to the pickup shelf
blocks.html:

blocks.text: At the desk or a self-checkout kiosk, the member card and each copy are scanned. The system checks the member's limits, then writes a loan record with a due date.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 What happens at each step of a checkout

items: A copy on hold for another member cannot be checked out, even if it is on the shelf.
The receipt lists each copy with its due date.
A loan can be renewed twice unless someone is waiting for the copy.

blocks.text: Hold notices go out early in the morning, before any branch opens. Returns left in the book drop overnight are checked in before the desk opens, so a returned copy can fill a hold the same day.

blocks.caption: Figure 3 When each service runs during a weekday

views.label: All services
views.say: The book drop never closes; staffed hours are the shortest.

views.label: With staff
views.say: Notices go out at 6:00 and members can collect from 9:00.

views.label: Without staff
views.say: Kiosks and the book drop cover the hours around the desk.

bands.label: Staffed desk
bands.tip: Checkouts, renewals, card sign-ups, and hold pickups

bands.label: Kiosks open
bands.tip: Checkouts and renewals with a member card

bands.label: Open all day
bands.tip: Returns are accepted at any hour

dots.label: Emptied
dots.tip: Staff check in the night's returns before the desk opens

dots.label: Sent
dots.tip: An email or text names the pickup branch and the last pickup day

blocks.title: Copies in transit
blocks.text: A copy returned at another branch travels back by van. It shows as in transit and cannot fill a hold until it arrives.

sections.title: Who can borrow
sections.nofigure: Three card types compared on a few limits; the cards and the table already show them side by side.

blocks.text: Anyone who lives, works, or studies in the area can get a card. The card type sets how many items a member can have at once.

items.label: Under 13
items.title: Child card
items.text: A parent or guardian signs for the card and is told about overdue items.

blocks.title: Expired cards
blocks.text: A card that expired more than a year ago is renewed only at a desk, with proof of address.

tabs.label: Returns and fines
tabs.title: Returning a book
tabs.lead: A returned copy is checked in, the loan is closed, and the copy goes to the next member or back to the shelf.

blocks.text: Loans used to last two weeks. At the start of 2022 the library moved to three weeks, which gave members time to finish longer books without renewing.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 When the loan period changed and which years the return figures cover

learn.label: 2-week loans
learn.tip: Loans from 2018 to the end of 2021 lasted two weeks

test.label: Years in the return figures
test.tip: Figure 2 counts returns from these three years

items: Loans that started before the change kept their two-week due date.
The return figures start in 2023, a full year after the change, so every loan in them is a three-week loan.

blocks.text: Daily fines were dropped in 2023. Instead, borrowing pauses once an item is 30 days overdue, and reminders go out before the due date.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 Late returns per 1,000 loans, by reminder

bars.label: Email and text
bars.tip: Members who added a phone number

blocks.text: The system looks at the member's oldest overdue loan each time a copy is scanned.
A copy that is lost or comes back damaged is charged at a flat rate.
Every pickup branch has a hold shelf with fixed space. Each morning staff remove holds that were not collected within 7 days, which makes room for the copies that arrive that day.

blocks.caption: Figure 3 Hold shelf space before and after the morning sweep

items.label: Expired
items.tip: Holds past 7 days; most go back to the shelf

blocks.title: Scan before moving
blocks.text: Scan a copy before moving it to another shelf. The member's notice names the shelf, so an unscanned move sends the member to the wrong place.
